conversion: Decoded with FFmpeg to mono 44100 Hz signed 16-bit PCM WAV; no content processing (no EQ, no level change, no effects) was applied to the bundled files. The HaelDB clips were downmixed stereo->mono and the cicifyre clips were converted 32-bit float->16-bit; that is format only. All trimming, segmentation, retuning, decay, and layering happen at render time in engine.py, so the bundled files stay comparable to what each source page serves.
verification: Every collection's licence was read from its own OpenGameArt source page (not from a search result and not from a mirror), and each download's SHA-256 is recorded as retrieved. The repo has been burned before by mirror-vs-source licence mismatches, so a search hit was never treated as a licence.

excluded.name: 11 male human pain/death sounds (Michel Baradari)
excluded.reason: The obvious first hit for a human pain/death voice, and exactly the kind of thing to reach for. Licensed CC-BY 3.0 on its own OpenGameArt page (author Michel Baradari, submitted by qubodup), which fails the CC0-only policy. Rejected on licence, not on quality.

excluded.name: VoiceBosch audio packs (EFFORT / DAMAGE / DEATH, male)
excluded.reason: A whole family of high-quality male effort, damage, and death vocalizations (also on itch.io as VoiceBosch). Every one is CC-BY-SA 4.0 on its own OpenGameArt page -- confirmed on the EFFORT and DEATH pages -- so all three fail the CC0-only policy. Would have covered effort and death outright; rejected on licence.

excluded.name: SpliceSound - female inhale/exhale/sigh breathing (Freesound 218309)
excluded.reason: The cleanest candidate found for the `breath` cue. Freesound gates the download master behind a login and serves only a lossy preview; policy forbids bundling a lossy preview as if it were a master, and OpenGameArt had no clean CC0 isolated breath. So `breath` is left ABSENT in engine.py -- it refuses to render and names this recording -- rather than approximated from a grunt tail. Reach for a downloaded CC0 breath master to lift it.

excluded.name: creature_foley_generator's grunt / hurt / breath cues
excluded.reason: Not a licensing exclusion. It has pain, defeat, breath, and grunt cues, but they are built from a rubberduck CREATURE library -- monster vocalizations, not human. Fantasy Adventure's player/hurt prompt is explicit: 'a single very brief nonverbal HUMAN pain grunt ... No monster voice.' Kept here so nobody wires the creature grunts into a human hurt and wonders why it reads as a monster.

collections.name: grunts of male death and pain
collections.author: thebardofblasphemy
collections.note: ~50 s of one man's voice 'attempting to sound injured or dying', ~19 grunts and groans separated by silence. The primary hurt and death bank; engine.py cuts individual grunts out of it at render time.

collections.name: Male Grunt/Yelling sounds
collections.author: HaelDB
collections.license: CC0 (source page also offers OGA-BY 3.0; used here under CC0)
collections.selection: Nine of ~60: the six short grunts (3grunt1-6), used for hurt and effort, and one yell from each of three vocalists (1yell1/2yell1/3yell1) for shout. The screams were left for a future scream cue. Recorded on a Neumann mic + Avalon preamp per the source page. Dual-licensed OGA-BY 3.0 / CC0 on its own page; where a work is offered under multiple licences the user may choose one, and CC0 is chosen and recorded here.

collections.name: Female RPG Voice Starter Pack
collections.author: cicifyre
collections.selection: Six of ~90: only the wordless reactions from Type 1 -- damaged1-3 (a hurt reaction) and jump1-3 (an effort reaction). At ~0.3 s each they are far too short to be the spoken word 'damaged'; they are grunts. The spell names (fire, heal, aqua, ...) and the spoken action lines are speech and were deliberately left out: this is a non-verbal generator. The female voice for hurt and effort.
